correctness.rationale: Fourier inversion shows that when two vectors differ only in coordinate c, every mode with j_c=0 cancels. The real pole order is then maximized by zeroing every unchanged coordinate. For l_c=2 the unique dominant surviving pole is real of order 1-2/phi(M), with a positive Selberg-Delange constant, so the sign stabilizes. For l_c at least 3 the dominant pair is conjugate and nonzero, giving the stated cosine law. In the explicit M=5, l=(3,2,1,1) case the pole orders are exactly 1/2 and 1/8 plus or minus i sqrt(3)/8, proving an eventual positive main term.

originality.rationale: The inspected Tang preprint conjectures infinite sign changes for every distinct pair in the section treating systems with some modulus at least 3, but does not identify the changed-coordinate obstruction. Searches of the arXiv identifier, source title, mixed-modulus squarefree races, and the explicit (3,2,1,1) pattern did not locate a prior correction. Porritt's earlier scalar omega-mod-q race gives related Selberg-Delange and log-log-density methodology but not this vector-valued mixed-modulus problem. The source's recency leaves residual concurrent-work risk.

value.rationale: The result supplies a rigorous counterexample to a new universal conjecture and explains the mechanism: unchanged high-modulus coordinates disappear from the leading Fourier race. It also replaces the failed heuristic with a complete one-coordinate dichotomy, separating stable binary races from oscillatory races of modulus at least three.
